report:
The unchanged submission is not certified. I found no concrete mathematical counterexample to the reconstructed curve argument, but essential original-source applications and the required whole-file audit remain unresolved. This is a whole-submission INCONCLUSIVE verdict, not acceptance of Theorem B, Lemma C, Theorem A, or the five notes separately.

The exposed read-only interfaces did not provide access to the complete frozen local TeX, argument, ledger, scope document, or original 62-file binder. I therefore cannot certify independent reading of all 1105 TeX lines, all 399 argument lines, every ledger application, or their equality with the frozen source. Public retrieval supplied pertinent literal BPR v1, CLD v1, FK v5, BE v3 and Stacks text. Retrieval did not supply the required original RG scan, BL85 scan, or Berkovich1993 comparison proof. External premise indices 4, 8 and 9 consequently have no independently verified primary quotation below. Metadata, quotations in later sources, source bindings and earlier reviewers' descriptions do not discharge those obligations. The quotations supplied for other indices are short identifying excerpts; they do not imply that every recursively cited foundation was reconstructed.

I used exactly the eight task-authorized grants with their supplied qualifications. O supplies the actual operator and extended-energy laws, not prescribed-target existence. D descends already invariant singular metrics and supplies the unique invariant Radon lift, not an inverse. M supplies the intrinsic target equivalence and finite-U coercivity; its supporting inequality gives attainment only after a genuine output is known. Its moment estimate cannot be transferred to the independently constructed theta*. N's norming-atom hypothesis remains conditional. T handles the trivial-valuation boundary; Q and G retain their projective-line and genus-zero scopes. C supplies locality and comparison without supplying the new all-genus inverse. The failed198/250 verdict, later working routes, hashes, builds and execution metadata were not mathematical grants.

For the reconstructed horizontal Cartier implication, the all-j argument is internally coherent once an actual bounded formal-etale evaluation chart isolating the residual root is established. The maximal ideal of R/varpi^j is nil without needing a uniform nilpotence exponent. Its extension to an algebra is nil element by element. The isolated residual fibre therefore has one point. Its affine etale evaluation section is open and closed and hence exhausts that fibre. Monicity makes t-c regular on the polynomial chart; flat etale base change preserves regularity. Unique compatible quotients modulo every varpi^j, followed by completeness and separation, establish the closed exact evaluation ideal (t-c). This preserves the original generic point p and gives residual intersection length one. These calculations do not themselves establish the existence of the required actual chart or authorize algebraization of an unknown formal carrier.

The vertical construction has the correct conditional algebra. With the outgoing Laplacian convention, the negative quadratic form is the sum of squared edge differences divided by edge lengths. Shared Gamma-valued vertex heights close every cycle. Rational slopes p<s<q and the stated bend position preserve exact endpoints and give positive new degree q-p. Small incidence errors preserve positive old degrees; loops require both incidences. The actual factors c_v*x^m have integral unit overlap ratios when the endpoint equation is satisfied. The inverse frame gives the claimed metric sign, and the two residual branch orders are +m and -m. The generic bundle remains the original bundle. Every normalization must retain the full d*N*k denominator. An edgeless graph is a separate immediate case, rather than an application of a positive-valence error bound.

The reconstructed whole-mod-varpi generation argument correctly separates the non-Noetherian and Noetherian steps. Proper field-fibre component positivity gives fibre ampleness, and general Stacks 0D2S applies over the one-point quotient. Noetherian 30.21.4 is not applied directly there. The actual scheme, invertible bundle and inverse/evaluation maps must descend together; properness, locally finitely presented flatness and ampleness must hold at one later finite-Z-subalgebra stage. Aligning the finite section powers before descending an affine cover is necessary. At that stage, 01Q3 and 0B5T supply generation and higher vanishing for one sufficiently high k. The bounded nonnegative affine Cech complex has flat terms. Downward induction from its top degree makes its kernels flat and its short exact sequences universally exact, so tensoring with the possibly nonflat map to R/varpi preserves the required H0 and higher exactness. This does not justify a general perfect-complex shortcut.

The subsequent exact sheaf layers, compatible finite section lifts, complete-frame equalizers and integral geometric series establish formal sections with maximum norm one at every analytic point, conditional on that actual model and bundle. The remaining bridge is essential: these must be sections of H0 of the already original algebraic X with the same full d*N*k bundle. The printed adhesive FK comparison has the relevant stronger domain, but its immediate RG application and the same-carrier rigid/Berkovich H0 identification are not independently certified here. In particular, the required quotient flatness is over R/varpi, not over its polynomial algebra. Without this bridge, the proposed unconditional original-bundle FS recognition in Theorem B and note n2 remains unestablished.

The canonical-residue argument does more than invoke a singleton reduction fibre. Under the actual integral canonical-reduction and type-II hypotheses, divisibility of the ground value group gives ground-valued spectral norms. Normalizing elements by those norms and multiplying their nonzero reductions proves multiplicativity. Approximation in the completion of the honest fraction field with error less than one then identifies the whole completed residue field's residue with the component function field. The applicability of these hypotheses to every required actual chart remains part of the unresolved whole-source application audit.

The retrieved CLDv1 proof explicitly uses differences of generated residual bundles, and its calibrated-cone calculation addresses the coefficient rather than merely atomic support. Thus signed and zero coefficients have a substantive source route; positivity cannot silently be imposed at degree-zero refinement vertices. On a smooth, good, separated, boundaryless pure curve, the coefficient calculation must use the actual residual bundle and the established residual field, with value index one. A germ of definition dimension zero contributes zero. Global FS recognition and global smooth approximation are still needed to identify the measure with O's genuine operator. Local approachability alone is insufficient. These application dependencies prevent certification of the signed formula used in uniqueness, despite the pertinent CLD text having been inspected.

Conditional on actual FS recognition and genuine raw coefficients, Lemma C's construction has the required order of proof. Finite type-II atoms are inserted as actual vertices, and mixing must be strictly positive at every vertex before the Cartier construction. Uniform FS approximation with decreasing shifts gives an actual bounded continuous endpoint, hence E1 membership, before O identifies its measure. Removing the mixing and then approximating arbitrary graph Radon measures by mass-preserving type-II atoms uses joint kernel continuity. A nonatomic graph potential is not thereby piecewise linear, and it cannot be declared psh before this recognition.

The graph and compact-space steps can be checked without a countable-cofinality assumption. Compatible finite skeleta retain the cycles; their retractions separate points. Finite minima and maxima of factor functions, using compactness twice, uniformly approximate continuous functions. Consequently f composed with r_j converges uniformly to f. Grounded conductance inversion has the sign Delta_out j=delta_xi-delta_y, is symmetric and nonnegative, and respects subdivision, loops and parallel edges. Attaching a tree adds the common initial depth in that tree to the old kernel at the retractions, proving monotonicity. These facts support the retraction weak limit for arbitrary-support Radon targets.

After genuine finite inverses are established, the displayed raw energy identities are consistent: E(u_j)=(I00-I_j(mu,mu))/2, integral u_j dmu=-I_j(mu,mu)+C0, and F_mu(u_j)=(I_j(mu,mu)-2*C0+I00)/2. The cross terms cancel by kernel symmetry. Finite continuous dual energy therefore bounds I_j and gives a uniform lower energy bound. This uses M's finite-dual criterion and bounded reference covariance, not a moved reference moment or M0-alone coercivity. The literal set of FS majorants with a strictly positive everywhere gap is downward directed by a compact directed open-cover argument. Uniform approximation and small shifts give its exact infimum. O's extended-energy continuity applies before E1 membership; only afterward may its decreasing-measure law produce the prescribed target. Supporting attainment follows after that inverse.

The every-solution argument also has a coherent conditional structure, but depends essentially on the unverified original BL85 node calculation and signed actual-model trace applications. Each finite algebraic FS system must have an actual marked finite carrier. Basepoint freeness supplies an order-zero term that dominates on an entire sufficiently small tail ball, not only on a punctured ray. Real-weight type-III switches must remain. Signed Cartier recognition for already-FS tests yields the trace law; attached-tree cancellation and bounded-kernel uniform passage handle arbitrary real weights. For an already E1 solution, O's integrability against the genuine reference measure with a positive anchor atom proves a finite anchor. It does not prove that all E1 potentials are finite everywhere. Weak output convergence and a compact kernel-test family give uniform finite-graph traces. Positive future curvature and flat tails give radial inequalities and the exact infimum identity for each FS test. Commuting the two actual infima then establishes equality at type-I and type-IV endpoints and poles, conditional on the preceding carrier and trace statements. USC or almost-everywhere uniqueness alone would not establish this conclusion.

The reconstructed field descent uses the correct normalization. The absolute solution must be normalized relative to the invariant pullback of the original reference. Equivariance and every-solution all-point uniqueness then imply singular invariance before D is applied. D's unique invariant lift identifies the pulled-back operators of arbitrary downstairs solutions, and quotient surjectivity transfers their all-point equality. No singular averaging, field-degree factor, probability normalization or factorial scaling is justified or needed. This descent remains conditional on the unresolved upstairs theorem.

The five notes have the same dependency boundary: n1 registers grants; n2 contains the essential new recognition and curvature assertions; n3 depends on n2 for its genuine inverse; n4 depends on those assertions and the finite-carrier trace law; n5 records diagnostics rather than analytic proof. I did not reproduce the stated programs, grids or builds. The small displayed arithmetic examples are consistent, including the nonatomic interval's I=25/147 and E=-25/294, but this does not certify the formal or analytic arguments. Backend metadata neither changes nor independently certifies the parent's frozen invocation.

Harmless clarifications are to read affine invertible modules as rank-one projective modules, name the Cech kernels explicitly, handle the edgeless graph separately, count both loop incidences, retain integral unit ratios rather than literal equality to one, and omit zero coefficients at poles. The quotient-flatness distinction must remain explicit. The already supplied BE8.6 sign clarification preserves its absolute-value estimate. None of these readings supplies the missing comparison or carrier theorem, and no substantial repair or source edit was made.

Recursive dependencies include stable reduction, Tate/BGR affinoid and reduction foundations, EGA approximation and coherent cohomology, RG flatness, FK formal comparison/localization, and CLD's tropical calibration and stable Gauss-field arguments. I do not claim fresh reconstruction of all those foundations. Because the required complete frozen-source reading and essential immediate original proofs remain unresolved, PASS is unavailable. No concrete defect established here warrants FAIL. The proposed curve theorem remains unaccepted, and the original higher-dimensional nontrivial inverse, attainment and every-point uniqueness problem remains open.

passages.statement: Over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, a smooth projective connected curve with finitely many distinct rational marks has a marked semistable vertex set and an associated actual semistable formal model. Finite prescribed type-II points and further subdivisions can be incorporated by refinement; the model is constructed from canonical affinoid models and has the corresponding marked reductions and ordinary-node charts (BPR, arXiv:1404.0279v1, §§3–4).
passages.quote: There exists a semistable vertex set of X.

passages.statement: For a smooth projective connected curve over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued field, the finite semistable skeleta form a directed system with compatible retractions, their union contains precisely the type-II and type-III points, and the natural map from the entire analytification to their inverse limit is a homeomorphism (BPR v1, Corollary 5.1 and Theorem 5.2).
passages.quote: is a homeomorphism of topological spaces

passages.statement: On a semistable skeleton adapted to the divisor of a nonzero rational function on such a curve, its logarithmic absolute value factors through the associated punctured retraction, is piecewise affine with integral slopes, and its branch slopes are the corresponding orders of the reduced rational function; at a marked puncture its terminal slope is its algebraic order (BPR v1, §§2.10–2.13 and Theorem 5.15).

The vertex affinoids in BPR's canonical-model construction are strict affinoids with canonical models given by their power-bounded functions; after avoiding loop incidences their reductions are affine opens of the corresponding smooth residual component and have the vertex as their unique type-II Shilov point. In the edgeless case an appropriate open ball can be removed to obtain the vertex affinoid (BPR v1, §§4.1–4.15).

Let f be an adic morphism of adic formal schemes of finite ideal type, and let the target have a finitely generated ideal of definition I. Then f is etale if and only if every induced morphism modulo I^(j+1), j≥0, is etale (Fujiwara–Kato, arXiv:1308.4734v5, I.5.3.10–I.5.3.11).

An a-adically complete valuation ring V with nonzero a in its maximal ideal is topologically universally adhesive, as are topologically finitely generated V-algebras. Over a complete topologically universally adhesive adic ring A of finite ideal type, for U=Spec(A)\V(I), a proper morphism of separated finite-type U-schemes and a coherent sheaf satisfy rigid-analytification comparison for every coherent higher direct image, including q=0 (Fujiwara–Kato v5, 0.9.2.7, I.2.1.4(2), II.9.4.1–II.9.4.2, in the printed adhesive proof domain).

An a-adically complete valuation ring V with nonzero a in its maximal ideal is topologically universally adhesive, as are topologically finitely generated V-algebras. Over a complete topologically universally adhesive adic ring A of finite ideal type, for U=Spec(A)\V(I), a proper morphism of separated finite-type U-schemes and a coherent sheaf satisfy rigid-analytification comparison for every coherent higher direct image, including q=0 (Fujiwara–Kato v5, 0.9.2.7, I.2.1.4(2), II.9.4.1–II.9.4.2, in the printed adhesive proof domain).
passages.quote: is an isomorphism for all q ≥ 0.

passages.statement: Let (Y,Z) be a universally adhesive pair of algebraic spaces with Y universally cohesive, let f:X→Y be proper and finitely presented, let W=f^(-1)(Z), and let F be coherent on X. The completed higher direct image, the higher direct image on the formal completions, and the inverse limit of the higher direct images of F/I^(j+1)F are canonically bicontinuously isomorphic for every q≥0, with the topologies specified by the ideal and quotient filtrations (Fujiwara–Kato v5, Situation I.9.1.2 and Theorem I.9.2.1).

An etale morphism of schemes is flat and locally finitely presented; etaleness is preserved by base change, and its fibres over fields are disjoint unions of spectra of finite separable field extensions (Stacks, §41.11, Tag 02GH).
Every section of an unramified separated morphism of schemes is an open and closed immersion (Stacks, Proposition 41.6.1, Tag 024T).
passages.quote: Any section of an unramified separated morphism is open and closed.

passages.statement: For a Cartesian morphism of arbitrary thickenings (X⊂X')→(Y⊂Y'), with both induced morphisms locally of finite type, X→Y is proper if and only if X'→Y' is proper; arbitrary thickenings need not have globally nilpotent defining ideals (Stacks, Lemma 37.3.4, Tag 0BPG).
passages.quote: $f$ is proper if and only if $f'$ is proper

passages.statement: For a proper scheme of dimension at most one over a field, an invertible sheaf is ample if and only if its degree is positive on every one-dimensional irreducible component (Stacks, Lemma 33.44.15, Tag 0B5Y).

If f:X→Y is proper, L is invertible on X, and L restricted to the fibre at y is ample, then an open neighbourhood V of y exists on which L is relatively ample; no Noetherian hypothesis on Y is required (Stacks, Lemma 37.50.3, Tag 0D2S).

For a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps, finite locally free and invertible sheaves on the limit descend to a stage; the inverse sheaf and evaluation isomorphism for an invertible sheaf can be descended at a common sufficiently late stage (Stacks, Lemma 32.10.3, Tag 0B8W).
passages.quote: And after increasing $i$ further, we may assume it is an isomorphism.

If its base change to the limit is proper, its base change to some later stage is proper (Stacks, Lemma 32.13.1, Tag 081F).
passages.quote: then there exists an $i$ such that $f_ i$ is proper.

passages.statement: In a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated bases with affine transitions, let f0:X0→Y0 be locally finitely presented between finitely presented schemes over an initial base. If its base change to the limit is flat, its base change to some later stage is flat (Stacks, Lemma 32.8.7, Tag 04AI).

passages.statement: For a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transitions, an invertible sheaf on an initial stage whose pullback to the limit is ample has ample pullback at some later stage (Stacks, Lemma 32.4.15, Tag 09MT).

If X is quasi-compact and L is ample invertible, then X is quasi-separated and, for every finite-type quasi-coherent sheaf F, F⊗L^n is globally generated for all sufficiently large n. The generating sections can be chosen in a finite list (Stacks, Proposition 28.27.13, Tag 01Q3).
passages.quote: is globally generated for all $n \geq n_0$

passages.statement: If R is Noetherian, X→Spec(R) is proper, L is ample invertible and F is coherent, then every H^q(X,F) is a finite R-module and H^q(X,F⊗L^d)=0 for all q>0 and all sufficiently large d (Stacks, Lemma 30.16.1, Tag 0B5T).

If R is Noetherian, X→Spec(R) is proper, L is ample invertible and F is coherent, then every H^q(X,F) is a finite R-module and H^q(X,F⊗L^d)=0 for all q>0 and all sufficiently large d (Stacks, Lemma 30.16.1, Tag 0B5T).

For a Cartesian directed system of finitely presented ring-algebra-module data (R_lambda→S_lambda,M_lambda), if the colimit module is flat over the colimit base ring, then M_lambda is flat over R_lambda for all sufficiently large lambda (Stacks, Lemma 10.168.1(3), Tag 02JO).

On a good separated smooth boundaryless pure analytic curve over a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field, a globally approachable PL metrized line bundle has its genuine curvature coefficients given by the degree of its residual germ bundle at definition-dimension-one points; definition-dimension-zero germs contribute zero. Residual bundles may be expressed as differences of generated bundles, so the coefficient identity applies to signed and zero degrees. Actual formal restriction identifies the residual bundle, and the algebraically closed value-index factor is one (CLD, arXiv:1204.6277v1, §§6.5.1, 6.6.8, 6.8.2–6.8.3 and 6.9.2–6.9.6, including Lemma 6.9.5).

On the projective geometrically reduced carrier and semiample rational bundle of Boucksom–Eriksson's continuous theory, every psh metric is psh-regularizable; continuous psh metrics admit uniform smooth semipositive regularization. The genuine continuous mixed measures extend the smooth operator by uniform-to-weak continuity and retain the raw intersection mass (arXiv:1805.01016v3, Theorem 7.14 and §§8.3–8.7).
